structure.overview: This case concerns the tax treatment of compensation paid to non-resident athletes Martin and Donaldson, specifically the allocation and inclusion of Registered Retirement Compensation Arrangement (RCA) contributions in taxable income under the Income Tax Act. The Crown appealed the Tax Court's decision, which had sided with Martin and Donaldson by allowing their appeals against reassessments and excluding RCA contributions from taxable income after allocating 40% of total compensation to Canadian duties. The Federal Court of Appeal dismissed the Crown's appeals, affirming the Tax Court's approach and interpretation of the Act.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Martin and Donaldson, non-residents, performed 60% of duties in the US and 40% in Canada; employer paid to RCAs excluded from income under the Act.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Martin and Donaldson allocated 40% of total compensation to Canadian services but reported only salary portion as taxable income, excluding RCA contributions.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Minister applied the Act to salary only (excluding RCA contributions) then allocated 40% to Canada, resulting in lower taxable income than taxpayers claimed.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Tax Court agreed with Martin and Donaldson's approach and allowed their appeals against reassessments.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Crown appeals the Tax Court decision, maintaining the Minister's approach is correct.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court will dismiss the appeals and notes amounts are stated in US dollars but must be converted to Canadian dollars for tax purposes.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Westcoast Actuaries' report reasonably estimated RCA contributions for Martin based on 40% Canadian income; date corrected to 2015; Crown does not dispute amounts.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Martin's UPC amended in 2015 to reflect RCA; payments made in 2015-2017 include salary, playoff bonus, and RCA contributions as per agreement.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Payments to Martin and RCA include deductions; total matches agreed salary and bonuses in UPC.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Donaldson's UPC for 2016-2017 sets salary amounts excluding playoff bonuses.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Westcoast Actuaries' report reasonably estimated RCA contributions for Donaldson based on 40% Canadian income; Crown does not dispute amounts.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Donaldson's UPC amended in 2016 to reflect RCA; payments made in 2016-2017 include salary, playoff bonus, and RCA contributions as per agreement.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Payments to Donaldson and RCA include deductions; total matches agreed salary and playoff bonuses in UPC.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Part XI.3 imposes refundable tax on RCA custodian; employer must deduct and remit this tax when paying RCA contributions.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Refundable tax equals 50% of contributions plus 50% of RCA income exceeding losses minus 50% of distributions.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Refundable tax is refunded when RCA distributions are made, which are then taxed or withheld accordingly.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Club deducted and remitted refundable tax for all RCA payments made.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Tax Court noted Act taxes non-residents on taxable income earned in Canada per Division D, subsection 2(3).

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Tax Court referred to place-by-place income determination for employees performing duties in multiple locations under paragraph 4(1)(b).

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Tax Court found RCA contributions were part of compensation for duties performed in Canada by Martin and Donaldson.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Tax Court concluded Canadian-sourced compensation is 40% of total, then RCA contributions excluded from income under the Act.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Crown argues Tax Court erred by including 40% of RCA contributions in income before deducting them under subparagraph 6(1)(a)(ii).

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court rejects Crown's characterization; Tax Court excluded RCA contributions from income after isolating Canadian-sourced compensation.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Standard of review is correctness because issue is statutory interpretation.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Supreme Court summarized modern statutory interpretation principles in Piekut v. Canada.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Section 2 of the Act distinguishes residents and non-residents; non-residents taxed only on income earned in Canada per subsection 2(3).

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Subparagraph 115(1)(a)(i) limits non-resident taxable income to income from duties performed in Canada.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Crown argues taxable income earned in Canada is 40% of total income excluding RCA contributions, so RCA contributions don't factor into allocation.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court finds text does not require applying Act to entire compensation before allocation; Act applies only to Canadian-sourced compensation.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Applying Act to entire compensation then allocating 40% would tax more than 40% of compensation, including US duties, which is incorrect.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court illustrates the Crown's tax interpretation on total compensation including RCA contributions for Russell Martin and Josh Donaldson with detailed tables.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court rejects the Crown's view that RCA contributions are not compensation for Canadian duties, affirming the Tax Court's finding that they are.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds evidence supports that RCA payments were part of compensation for duties performed in Canada, based on actuarial assumptions of 40% Canadian duties.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains that UPCs were amended to divert salary to RCAs, with total yearly payments matching agreed compensation plus bonuses.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court reasons that RCA contributions logically represent compensation for Canadian duties, not U.S. duties.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court rejects the Crown's argument that RCA contributions shouldn't be considered due to different taxpayers and tax parts, affirming tax under the Act applies.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court holds RCA contributions and distributions are relevant as they replace salary and will be taxed, so should not alter compensation for Canadian services.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states statutory interpretation requires textual, contextual, and purposive analysis harmonized with the Act, citing Supreme Court precedents.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court agrees with Martin and Donaldson's and the Tax Court's approach to first determine compensation for Canadian duties, then income inclusion or exclusion.
